history of 1-2 paragraphs to each year with references and hyperlinks (look at established team/player pages for inspiration) |date=2024-07-18 }} ===Acquisiting of Samsung Galaxy and the creation of Gen.G Esports (2018)=== On November 30th, 2017, Samsung sold its Esports division, which included the ''League of Legends'' [[World_Championship/2017|2017 World Championship]] roster, [[:leagueoflegends:Samsung Galaxy|Samsung Galaxy]] to Silicon Valley-based esports firm '''{{abbr|KSV|Korea + Silicon Valley}}''' which was founded earlier in the year by Kevin Chou and Kent Wakeford, co-founders of the video game development company Kabam, Michael Li, and Phillip Hyun. {{cite web|url=https://www.koreaherald.com/view.php?ud=20171201000733|title=Samsung sells off eSports team to KSV|author=Shin Ji-hye|publisher=The Korea Herald|date=2017-12-01|language={{Flag|usuk}} English}} They participated in the [[LCK/2018/Spring|LCK 2018 Spring]] Split but were eliminated in the playoffs after falling 1-2 against [[SK Telecom T1]]. Following the split, they announced their rebranding in May, changing their name from KSV to '''Gen.G Esports'''. {{cite web|url=https://venturebeat.com/esports/ksv-esports-rebrands-as-gen-g-adds-clash-royale-team/|title=KSV Esports rebrands as Gen.G, adds Clash Royale team|author=Dean Takahashi|publisher=VentureBeat|date=2018-05-03|language={{Flag|usuk}} English}} Heading into [[LCK/2018/Summer|Summer]] Gen.G also added Moon "[[Mong]]" Chang-min, and Song "[[Fly_(Song_Yong-jun)|Fly]]" Yong-jun to their roster for the regular season. {{cite web|url=https://www.invenglobal.com/lol/articles/5085/geng-esports-lol-team-announces-their-new-recruits-fly-and-mong|title=GenG Esports LoL team announces their new recruits: Fly and Mong|author=Byungho "Haao" Kim|publisher=Inven Global|date=2018-05-17|language={{Flag|usuk}} English}} This time the team ended in 4th in the regular season, but saw a prompt exit after losing to the [[Afreeca Freecs]]. With their elimination, they now thad to go through the [[LCK/2018/Regional_Finals|Regional Finals]] as a last chance to go to [[Worlds 2018|Worlds]]. Starting off in the first round as the third seed, they were able to battle their way through, defating the likes of [[SK Telecom T1|SKT]], [[Griffin]] and [[KING-ZONE DragonX|DragonX]] to qualify as the last Korean representative. Their run at Worlds however would be dissapointing one. Falling way behind in the expectations had of the [[LCK]], the team was eliminated in the group stage, ending last in their group with a 1-5 record. To conclude the year, they would part ways with a large part of their roster as [[Ambition]], [[Haru]], [[Crown]], [[CoreJJ]], and [[Mong]] all took their leave, marking an end to the roster that won Worlds in 2017.{{cite web|url=https://x.com/GenG_KR/status/1063242158801473536|title=Farewell, Ambition and Crown|author=Gen.G Esports|date=2018-11-16|language={{Flag|usuk}} English}}{{cite web|url=https://www.facebook.com/100063473119865/posts/1063588377147504/|title=Our contracts with CoreJJ, Haru, & Mong have come to an end.|author=Gen.G Esports|date=2018-11-17|language={{Flag|usuk}} English}} ===(2019)=== The 2019 season saw Gen.G finishing in 7th place in [[LCK/2019/Spring|LCK Spring]] and 6th in [[LCK/2019/Summer|LCK Summer]], failing to qualify for [[World_Championship/2019|Worlds]]. In the 2020 season, they finished 2nd in [[LCK/2020/Spring|LCK Spring]] and reached the playoff stage of the Mid-Season Cup. They ended 3rd in [[LCK/2020/Summer|LCK Summer]] and secured a spot in [[World_Championship/2020|Worlds]] as the 3rd seed via the LCK 2020 Regional Finals. They reached the quarter-finals, but ended up losing to [[G2 Esports]]. ===(2021)=== In 2021, Gen.G finished 2nd in [[LCK/2021/Spring|LCK Spring]] but did not qualify for [[Mid-Season_Invitational/2021|MSI 2021]]. But in the 2022 [[LCK/2022/Summer|LCK Summer]] Split, Gen.G secured their first LCK championship by defeating [[T1]] in the finals with a 3-0 score, earning them the first seed for the [[World_Championship/2022|2022 World Championship]]. At Worlds, Gen.G performed well in the group stage, finishing first, and advanced to the quarter-finals where they beat [[DAMWON Gaming]] in a close 3-2 series. However, in the semi-finals, they faced [[DRX]] and lost the series 1-3. ===King of LCK, Paper Tiger in Internationals (2023)=== In [[LCK/2023/Spring|LCK Spring 2023]], Gen.G once again won the championship by defeating [[T1]] in the finals with a 3-1 score, securing their first seed for the [[Mid-Season_Invitational/2023|Mid-Season Invitational 2023]], alongside [[T1]]. The team finished {{Ordinal|4|sup=yes}} in the Bracket Stage of MSI, after losses to [[T1]] and [[Bilibili Gaming]]. On August 20th, Gen.G emerged victorious in [[LCK/2022/Summer|LCK Summer 2023]], achieving the second three-peat in the history of LCK, while also qualifying for [[World Championship/2023|Worlds]] as LCK's {{Ordinal|1|sup=yes}} seed. In the Swiss Stage, Gen.G were one of the two teams that advanced to the Quarterfinals without dropping a single match. The finalized bracket for the Knockout Stage seemed to favor Gen.G as well, with [[Peyz]] commenting "Luck is on our side."{{cite web|url=https://youtu.be/XYgeaW94960|title=Gen.G Quarterfinals Draw Reaction {{!}} Worlds 2023|publisher=[[Gen.G Esports]]|date=2023-10-30|language={{FlagNoLink|kr}} Korean}} However, Gen.G was eliminated by [[BLG]] in the quarterfinals with a 2-3 upset, and Peyz's comment was later interpreted as arrogance. {{Quote |quote=We were told Busan was the Church of Chovy but what's a god to five non-believers? BLG will face Weibo in Semis. |sign=[[Medic]] |source=Worlds 2023 Quarterfinals{{cite web|url=https://youtu.be/HzKEBz9oWX8|title="WHAT'S A GOD TO FIVE NON-BELIEVERS"|publisher=LoL Esports|date=2023-11-03}} }} ===First International Crown (2024)=== In [[LCK/2024/Spring|LCK Spring 2024]], Gen.G came out on top of the Group Stage, dropping only one match against [[KT Rolster]]. Their win streak continued, achieving the first 4-peat in the history of LCK.{{cite web|url=https://x.com/LCK/status/1779465354340950523|title=GAME, MATCH, 4-PEAT #LCK CHAMPIONSHIP for @GenG!|author=[[LCK]]|date=2024-04-14}} Their win streak continued in the [[Mid-Season Invitational/2024|MSI]], bringing back the MSI trophy to LCK for the first time in 7 years;{{cite web|url=https://x.com/LCK/status/1792187096720970031|title=BECOME THE CHAMPIONS|author=[[LCK]]|date=2024-05-19}} the first ever international trophy under the name Gen.G. Despite being swept by [[Top Esports|TES]] in the quarterfinals of [[EWC 2024]], Gen.G continued their win streak in the LCK, becoming the first team to qualify for [[World Championship/2024|Worlds]] via the MSI champion seed.{{cite web|url=https://x.com/LCK/status/1813918619711254900|title=Congratulations on the incredible #LCK record, @GenG!|author=[[LCK]]|date=2024-07-27}}{{cite web|url=https://x.com/lolesports/status/1817166758907666741|title=WELCOME TO #WORLDS2024|author=LoL Esports|date=2024-07-27}} ==Gallery== ===Rosters=== GENG Worlds 2020.jpg|Gen.G at [[World_Championship/2020|Worlds 2020]]
